claims.claim: The word tomorrow comes from it being the first direction the arrow of time takes humans on Earth.
claims.note: This is linguistically and scientifically incorrect; tomorrow is a word for the future day, not a physical direction of the arrow of time.

claims.claim: The use of terms like tomorrow and now is part of the a-series view of time.
The a-series view is part of the presentism philosophy of time.
For a young child, tomorrow is an undefined, infinite time of the idea that time is just an arbitrary definition of an yet unidentified of what we like to call time.
claims.note: This statement is grammatically incoherent and philosophically confused.

claims.claim: Children slowly learn to understand and use the terms tomorrow and now.
Our heart is the powerhouse of your body.
It pumps blood throughout your body.
It carries oxygen and nutrients to all the parts of your body.
It keeps you alive and functioning.
It helps regulate your heart rate.
claims.note: The heart does not regulate its own rate directly; heart rate is regulated by the nervous system and electrical impulses from the sinoatrial node.

claims.claim: Regulating heart rate helps keep your blood pressure stable.
Regulating heart rate keeps your heart strong.
claims.note: Maintaining appropriate heart rate is part of normal cardiovascular function, but the phrasing is somewhat imprecise regarding what directly strengthens the heart muscle.

claims.claim: A moisturizer is like a super-hero for your skin.
A moisturizer helps keep your skin soft and smooth.
A moisturizer protects your skin from the sun.
claims.note: Standard moisturizers do not protect against the sun unless they explicitly contain sunscreen.

claims.claim: A moisturizer protects your skin from harsh environmental factors.
Scientists study how air and water move.
Scientists study how plants grow.
Scientists study how things break down.
Scientists study how electricity and magnets work.
Months are measured based on how long it takes for the Moon to orbit the Earth.
claims.note: Our calendar months do not correspond to the Moon's orbital period; they are arbitrary divisions of the solar year.

claims.claim: Lunar cycles are still used today to divide the year into 12 equal parts called months.
claims.note: Gregorian calendar months are not equal parts based on lunar cycles.

claims.claim: The Earth's rotation around the Sun has caused the Moon's orbit to slightly wobble, which means that some months are actually longer than others.
claims.note: Month lengths are historical leftovers from the Roman calendar and do not vary based on lunar orbital wobbles.

claims.claim: The Moon's orbit is tilted by about 5 degrees compared to our Earth's orbit.
The Moon passes through a different part of the Earth's shadow every time it goes around.
claims.note: The Moon only passes through Earth's shadow during lunar eclipses, not every orbit.

claims.claim: Electric cars are cars that run on electricity instead of gas
They have a rechargeable battery inside
When you turn the key, the motor turns and the battery powers the wheels
Electric cars are much quieter and cleaner than traditional gasoline cars because they don't burn fuel like gasoline does
They save you money on gas because they use electricity instead of oil
Planes fly in the sky because they have wings
Wings are like giant fans that help them fly
claims.note: Wings do not function like fans; they generate lift through airflow and shape.

claims.claim: Planes use the wind to push them up into the air and then lift them off the ground
claims.note: Planes generate their own airflow using engines, they do not rely on wind to lift them off the ground.

claims.claim: Planes are like little flying machines
The biggest planet in the Solar System is Jupiter.
Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun.
Jupiter is a gas giant because it is so large.
Jupiter is made mostly of gas.
The other gas giants in the Solar System are Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
Rhythm is the pulse or tempo of music.
claims.note: Rhythm is not tempo or the pulse; tempo is the speed and the pulse is the beat. Rhythm refers to the pattern of sounds and silences of different lengths.

claims.claim: Beat is the basic unit that measures rhythm.
A beat is the basic unit of music, like a ticking clock or a drumbeat.
Rhythm is how we hear and remember the music.
claims.note: Rhythm is technically the pattern of durations of notes, but saying it helps us remember the music is an acceptable poetic simplification for a child.

claims.claim: Beat is how the music moves us.
claims.note: A bit vague, but acceptable as a metaphorical description for young children.

claims.claim: Trains are actually pretty short.
claims.note: Trains are generally very long, consisting of many connected cars, contrary to being short.

claims.claim: They are built with a special design called a longitudinal shape, which means they have a lot of space between the cars.
claims.note: Trains do not feature a design called a longitudinal shape with large spaces between cars as described.

claims.claim: This helps them travel faster than trains with shorter designs, like the ones you might see in a car or bus.
claims.note: Cars and buses are not trains, and train length does not work this way.

claims.claim: Trains have to be very precise to avoid collisions, so they are designed to be very stable.
claims.note: While stability and collision avoidance are important in rail design, this phrasing is vague and incorrectly links stability to length and spacing mentioned earlier.

claims.claim: A pumpkin is usually orange.
claims.note: Standard pumpkins are orange.

claims.claim: A pumpkin can also be purple, red, blue, or white.
claims.note: There are heirloom and ornamental varieties of pumpkins in white, red, blue, and purple/grey tones.

claims.claim: The skin of a pumpkin is shiny and smooth.
claims.note: Pumpkin skin is typically dull, matte, and ribbed or bumpy rather than shiny and smooth.

claims.claim: The inside of a pumpkin is soft.
claims.note: The raw inside flesh is firm, though the stringy pulp and cooked flesh are soft.

claims.claim: The inside of a pumpkin is sweet.
claims.note: Raw pumpkin is not very sweet until cooked or prepared with sugar, but edible varieties do have a mild, naturally sweet flavor profile.

claims.claim: Singing in the shower is a way to get your body moving and loosen up.
The sound of water hitting the shower walls creates a natural rhythm.
The gentle pressure helps you focus on your breathing and release any tension.
Singing in the shower is a great way to get rid of any built-up steam before you step out.
claims.note: Singing does not remove steam from a bathroom; ventilation or condensation does.

claims.claim: We eat berries because they are full of juice and yummy seeds
Berries give us energy
Berries help keep our immune system strong
Berries help us sleep
Berries are a great way to get lots of vitamins and minerals from the food we eat
The Gregorian calendar was first adopted by most countries in the Western world.
The Julian calendar was used before the Gregorian calendar.
The Julian calendar didn't have a leap year.
claims.note: The Julian calendar actually did include leap years, adding a leap day every four years.

claims.claim: The Julian calendar would sometimes skip a year.
claims.note: The Julian calendar did not skip years; its issue was an overestimation of the solar year's length, leading to drift against the seasons over centuries.

claims.claim: Ice floats because it is super light.
claims.note: Ice floats due to density (being less dense than liquid water), not simply because it is light.

claims.claim: Ice is made up mostly of water.
Water is incredibly light compared to the air around it.
claims.note: Water is much denser and heavier than air.

claims.claim: Ice floats in a glass of water because it is lighter than the water.
claims.note: Being lighter in common parlance means weighing less, but buoyancy depends specifically on density.

claims.claim: Using public transportation, walking, or biking instead of driving alone reduces your carbon footprint.
Turning off and unplugging lights and electronics when not in use reduces your carbon footprint.
Using a reusable water bottle instead of buying plastic bottles reduces your carbon footprint.
Eating a plant-based diet reduces the carbon footprint of meat production.
Minimizing waste by recycling, composting, and using reusable bags reduces your carbon footprint.
A banana tastes like sweet fruit
A banana is juicy
claims.note: Bananas are generally starchy and creamy rather than juicy.

claims.claim: A banana has a mild flavor
A banana has a crunchy texture
claims.note: Bananas have a soft and creamy texture, not crunchy.

claims.claim: A hot air balloon floats in the sky because it is carrying warm air inside.
The warm air inside the balloon is lighter than the cold air around it.
The hot air rises and pushes the cold air down to make the balloon go up.
claims.note: Hot air rises due to buoyancy because it is less dense than the surrounding air, rather than actively pushing the cold air down as the primary mechanism for lift.

claims.claim: Friends make you feel happy because they share your interests, laugh with you, and offer you a safe space to be yourself.
When you are with friends, you feel seen, heard, and valued, which makes you feel good inside.
Having a budget helps you manage your money better by keeping track of how much you earn and how much you spend each month.
A budget helps you avoid overspending.
A budget helps you save money for emergencies.
A budget helps you make smart investments.
A budget gives you a clear picture of your finances so you can decide if you need to cut back on something or if you can afford to splurge on something special.
Fear of the dark happens because our brains and bodies are wired to protect us from danger.
When we feel alone or isolated in a dark room, our brain triggers a fight-or-flight response, which makes us feel scared.
Fear of the dark is a survival mechanism that helps keep us safe.
Galaxies are mostly made up of hot, glowing gas and dust.
claims.note: Galaxies are mostly made of dark matter, followed by stars, with gas and dust making up a relatively small percentage.

claims.claim: Gas and dust are what gives galaxies their bright colors.
claims.note: Galaxy colors are primarily determined by the light from their stars (such as young blue stars and old red stars), not the gas and dust.

claims.claim: The gas is mostly hydrogen and helium, but it also contains other elements like oxygen, carbon, and iron.
The dust is made up of tiny particles of silicon, carbon, and oxygen that are trapped inside giant clouds of gas.
Astronomers think that the dark matter that makes up most of the universe is also made up of these same particles.
claims.note: Dark matter is not made of standard dust particles (silicon, carbon, and oxygen); its true nature is unknown, but it is known to be non-baryonic or exotic.

claims.claim: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
Green is the secondary color made from mixing blue and yellow.
Green is also called teritary color because it is made by mixing two primary colors.
claims.note: Mixing two primary colors creates a secondary color, not a tertiary color. Tertiary colors are made by mixing a primary color with a secondary color.

claims.claim: Flowers are the reproductive parts of plants.
Flowers have petals.
Flowers sometimes have seeds inside them.
Some flowers are for pollen, and others are for seeds.
claims.note: Most individual flowers contain structures for both pollen and seeds rather than being strictly divided into separate categories for one or the other.

claims.claim: Food becomes spicy because of the heat.
claims.note: Food is spicy due to chemical compounds like capsaicin, not because of physical heat.

claims.claim: Cooking releases steam that carries heat and makes food taste hotter.
claims.note: Spiciness is a chemical sensation, not a result of steam or temperature from cooking.

claims.claim: Spicy foods are made with heat.
claims.note: Spiciness comes from chemical compounds in plants like chili peppers, not from heat.

claims.claim: Allergies happen when the immune system mistakes harmless things like pollen, dust, or even food proteins as foreign invaders.
When that happens, the body releases special chemicals called histamines to try to fight them off.
The immune cells mistake harmless things like pet dander or a little bit of yogurt for something dangerous.
Butterflies fly because they have strong wings.
claims.note: Butterfly wings are actually quite fragile, delicate, and thin, not strong in the sense implied.

claims.claim: Their wings are made of special flaps called chitin.
claims.note: Chitin is a tough material found in the exoskeleton, but butterfly wings are made of thin membranes supported by veins and covered in tiny scales, not made of 'flaps called chitin'.

claims.claim: Chitin is like a hard shell.
claims.note: Chitin is a primary component of arthropod exoskeletons, which function somewhat like a shell.

claims.claim: When the butterfly wants to fly, it flaps its wings and pushes off the ground with all its strength.
claims.note: Butterflies do not need to push off the ground with all their strength; many take off simply by dropping from a perch or flapping their wings to generate lift.

claims.claim: We have day and night because the Earth rotates around its axis.
When the Sun is at its highest point in the sky, it is daytime.
When it is at its lowest point, it is nighttime.
The Earth's rotation keeps our planet safe from extreme weather like hurricanes and tornadoes.
claims.note: The Earth's rotation does not protect it from hurricanes and tornadoes; in fact, Earth's rotation helps drive and shape hurricanes.

claims.claim: Rainbows happen when the sun shines through droplets of water in the sky.
When the drops hit the air, they bend the light waves like a rainbow.
claims.note: The bending of light is caused by refraction when light enters and exits the water droplets, not by the drops hitting the air.

claims.claim: The sun plays with the light and makes it look like rainbow colors.
Food sometimes smells funny because of a process called rancidification.
Rancidification is the process of complete or incomplete oxidation or hydrolysis of fats and oils when exposed to air, light, or moisture.
This can happen in food, especially if it's not stored properly or if it's been exposed to heat or light.
When these processes occur, undesirable odors and flavors can result.
In certain cases, the flavors can be desirable, as in aged cheeses.
